gitCommit.subject: An approval card follows its request on every channel, whatever settles it: answer elsewhere, expiry, cancelled run (#639)
gitCommit.body:
An approval card follows its request on every channel, whatever settles it: answer elsewhere, expiry, cancelled run (#639)

* Approval cards follow their request on every channel, whatever settles it

A card's message id was thrown away at send time, so only a tap on the card
itself could rewrite it. A request answered from the dashboard or another
channel, expired by the TTL sweep, or closed because its job tree was
cancelled left a dead card with live buttons in the owner's conversation
(found on an MCP-started job whose card went to Telegram).

Every card sent is now recorded (approval_card_messages, migration 0140), and
one state-driven point, settleApprovalCards, rewrites every unsettled card
whose request left pending: final text, buttons removed, on each channel that
can edit, and an explicit outcome + log for one that cannot (WhatsApp). It
runs right after any decision (resolveApprovalDecision) and on every cron
tick, which also catches requests settled outside the runner (web Stop).
Discord and Slack edits now drop their components/blocks like Telegram's.

Closes #637

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Type the fetch stub of the approval card test with its init argument

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Approval cards: a failed edit is retried then abandoned out loud, and a tap writes the card once

Review of #639 (pass 1):
- Channel editors (Telegram, Discord, Slack) now RETURN their outcome instead
  of swallowing it. A card is marked finished only after a successful edit
  (or when its channel cannot edit); a failed edit or missing credentials
  releases it for the next tick, up to APPROVAL_CARD_MAX_ATTEMPTS, then it is
  closed as gave_up with an explicit error log. Migration 0140 gains
  claimed_at (lease), attempts, last_error and outcome.
- The tick counts only cards actually rewritten, reports failed and
  non-editable ones separately, and a claim error reaches guardPhase.
- A tap on the card no longer writes it: the settlement point is the one
  writer, with one text (including "will now run without asking" and the
  brake caveat, read from the standing rule). Discord acknowledges the tap
  with deferUpdate; Slack is already acked.
- The Telegram always-allow flow re-reads the request after showing or
  restoring buttons, so a request settled in between never keeps live buttons.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prove the Back button of always-allow never leaves live buttons on a request settled meanwhile

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Approval cards: one function owns a card's display, under the settlement lease

Review of #639 (pass 2): card writers still lived outside the settlement
protocol (the Telegram handler's interactive edits and its rewrite-as-settled
fallback, which ignored the edit outcome).

- showApprovalCard is the only way to show an open card (the "Always allow?"
  question, "Back", "Still pending"): it adopts the card, takes it under the
  same claimed_at lease as settlement, re-reads the request, writes the
  settled text instead when the request is closed, takes the edit outcome
  into account, releases, then replays settlement so a decision that landed
  while the card was held is caught at once.
- A tap on a card of an already-settled request (gave_up, never recorded, or
  an edit that did not hold) puts it back in the settlement queue with
  attempts reset, on Telegram, Discord and Slack; a card never recorded is
  adopted (unique message key in 0140).
- Adapter edits take neutral buttons; Discord and Slack refuse buttons on an
  edit instead of sending the text alone.
- Discord acknowledges an approval tap before the decision and the card
  update; later ephemeral replies go out as follow-ups.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prove showApprovalCard never writes an asked view on a request already closed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Approval cards: an open card keeps Approve/Reject without an entity, and a failed replay never reaches the tap

Review of #639 (pass 3, minor findings):
- "Back" on a request without entity now shows Approve / Reject again: a
  pending card keeps its buttons; only "Always allow" needs an entity.
- showApprovalCard's final settlement replay is guarded like the one in
  resolveApprovalDecision: logged, left to the next tick, never thrown at
  the channel handler.
- The Discord interaction ack moves to interaction-ack.ts and is tested:
  an ephemeral reply is the initial response before acknowledge, a
  follow-up after it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* One allowlist of non-terminal runner senders, read by the architecture test and the bench

Each carried its own copy: approvals/card-settlement.ts, added to the runner
test's list, turned the bench's architecture section red in CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
